# N1-F2 verification — inactive adapter

Status: verified, awaiting user review. No N2 work is authorized.

The gate adds exactly 18 new files and edits no existing source. The fresh sequential baseline captured 1,520 files and 511 Git entries, verified exact originals, all predecessor package members and staged the unchanged baseline build before edits. Plugin data contained 175 History rows at this gate; that fresh observation replaces no historical evidence and authorizes no import.

The adapter is private and storage-free; its only runtime dependency is the new portable proof helper. Only tests implement the evidence provider, using actual validated captures, unchanged F1 analysis and actual N0 dispatch/projection. Actual Oath methods are exercised through a private projection seam. No production native reader, Oath routing, store opening, persisted Oath extension, enforcement, migration, installation or reload is included.

Preparation-before-completion is explicitly insufficient for durable Oath enrollment ordering. Positive cases are closed synthetic save-ack → open cut → completion only; uncertainty, deadline and latch behavior remain explicit. Full receipt/source/identity/Strict/Oath context never enters adapter snapshot callbacks. See `ItacanTaskCore/OATH-COMPATIBILITY.md` for the exact contract and limits.

All attempts, including failures, are retained. Initial provider tests exposed order-sensitive owner comparison; canonical comparison corrected it. The first child guard rejected Windows short/long Temp aliases; canonical resolution corrected the guard without broadening its boundary. An evidence-path normalization failure was corrected separately. Initial reporting serialized decorated PowerShell strings; final records use plain strings from raw files, with earlier attempts retained. Two new export tests initially named a nonexistent method; corrected to the actual unchanged `exportSharedPartition` API. None of these failed attempts establishes acceptance.

Exactly 18 new allowlisted files exist; all 511 original Git status entries remain, with 529 entries after this gate. No existing core, production source, prior report, frozen evidence, reader fixture or installed asset was edited. No live native CURRENT/RECOVERY/generation/fence/WRITER.lock artifacts were found outside backups.

All twelve before/after Temp build assets are byte-identical. Main/Atlas factory counts remain 168/24; production still constructs one Legacy Task Service. No F1/F2 adapter, native import writer or private codec was added to the startup graph. Nothing was installed and Obsidian was not launched, reloaded or restarted.

Four existing files changed during the gate: `.obsidian/workspace.json`, Hub `data.json`, `Resources/Knowledge/Tamos/Tasks.md`, and `Resources/Knowledge/Mathematics/MM7052 HT26, Topology/Tasks.md`. Their specific writer is unidentified. All test/build writes were guarded to OS Temp and implementation writes targeted only new allowlisted files. The changes were captured privately and preserved, never restored or attributed to a user action without evidence.

At the captured comparison, History rose from 175 to 177 rows and completion checks from three to five; every original History row remained. Changed plugin top-level fields were activityLog, completedTaskHistory, completedTaskChecks, hubState, workspaceMode and folderUi; a later final health pass additionally observed taskMetadata drift. Both capture stages are retained and no writer is inferred. Complete Oath/Strict/device state, Resource folders/mounts, Daily Brief and planning substates match the fresh baseline. Task-metadata identity, full plugin-data identity and all-Markdown identity are explicitly not claimed. Of 362 baseline Markdown files, the two listed notes changed; remaining baseline files outside the four classified paths match.

The first comparison correctly failed sensitive-state equality; a later check separately caught the additional taskMetadata drift. Both remain retained as failed attempts, with both classification records. The later Temp drift copy replaced the initial Temp snapshot copy; the archive therefore claims exact baseline and final captured bytes, not two independent complete intermediate snapshots. A separate final comparison validates unchanged scope/assets/source, retains sensitive differences as differences, and requires every changed path to have a recorded classification. No success claim relies on replacing a failed report or suppressing a mismatch.
